summary: Main AI compared all 30 source/translation pairs in the first calibration report and then read all 4 affected outputs after the targeted style update. This is overall calibration, not a claim of full-text correctness or sentence-perfect validation. All selected records have real saved output and all current tasks are done. The targeted rerun completed one batch with zero execution failures; it restores conditional if for the fever, removes the erroneous Don river name from ordinary town, makes young man a natural address, and removes unsupported elder-sister ordering. Narration is readable, dialogues mostly natural, UI concise, fixed names broadly consistent; BBCode and literal escapes have no reported structural mismatches. Nine current mechanical failed records mostly involve ordinary senses of rest/don/man/father/are/wolf/trade/thing/certain or words inside preserved runtime tokens, and are not a semantic error rate; they remain recorded, not silently passed in formal quality checks. Residual local wording can be handled by the mandatory full production review. Explicit remaining project issue: slash alternatives such as [Greedy:He/She] are still protected as whole tokens; visible-branch localization requires a separate documented project protection/repack treatment, preserving runtime actor/name identifiers. One initial output had a one-character ordinal-255 ID-suffix typo; the raw reply and hash are retained, canonical ID was restored only after unique ordinal/source/candidate comparison, and original batch-finish accepted the whole envelope. The pipeline now supports proceeding with the revised style, full production drafts, mechanical checks and independent review; this acceptance does not authorize final export or release without those gates.
